Inside the prototype

Bench supplies, spares & assembly tools

MB102 breadboard, perfboard/custom PCB, jumper wires, male headers and connectors, heat-shrink, cable ties, screws, soldering kit, hot glue/tape and multimeter are assembly aids. Use the 5 V / 2 A adapter and matching USB cable for programming or charger input. The spare red LED and unprotected Type-C TP4056 are not in the active circuit. SIM800L is optional and disconnected: current firmware uses Wi-Fi, with no cellular support.

Modules hidden in anti-static packaging cannot be verified from the photo alone. Housing dimensions are conceptual. Identified component features follow the Robu references; packaged variants remain approximate.

Robu: protected TP4056, SKU 53264, Mini-USB

Robu: SmartElex ESP32-WROOM-32E, R150542

Verified references: TP4056 connector and protection features; SmartElex model family and antenna. Boost R261487 could not be resolved in Robu search. Dimensions and hidden board variants are unverified. These are detailed visual approximations, not identical manufactured replicas.

Connection bench

Toggle a connection to test an open-circuit fault. Routes are fixed to our pin map; this is a rule-based wiring model.

WHAT THIS PREVIEW PROVES

Interactive 3D assembly and a JavaScript model of the local firmware rules. Firebase, Android notifications and collection emails are simulated; no messages are sent. It does not execute the ESP32 binary or simulate battery chemistry, power transients, acoustic reflections, enclosure sealing or component tolerances. Physical testing is still needed.

Build notes: Use the protected TP4056. Switch the load off while charging. Verify the boost output at 5.0 V. Never connect USB and boosted VIN simultaneously. Echo uses 20 kΩ above GPIO18 and 40 kΩ below it (two 20 kΩ resistors); nominal 3.33 V. Confirm delivered buzzer voltage, input polarity and board pin labels before assembly.
